Title: Ritual of Bitter Rose, Heidelburg Castle Qs.

Messages.Author: GP41
Messages.Body:
1) Can i play Ritual of Bitter Rose when diablerizing a vampire that
tried to leave torpor?

2) Can i play RoBR before a bloodhunt is called? And will it have any
effect?

3) Can i use Heidelburg Castle before a bloodhunt is called? I
remember someone answering no to that question. But I also remember
another person saying that any master card (i.e. Fragment of book of
Nood) can be tap during an action, to gain advantage of it's privilege.

GP41

Messages.Author: Gomi no Sensei
Messages.Body:
In article <3A088B26...@videotron.ca>, GP41 <GP...@videotron.ca> wrote:
>1) Can i play Ritual of Bitter Rose when diablerizing a vampire that
>tried to leave torpor?

The diablerizing minion isn't acting, and isn't in combat, so no. Alas.
Special cardtext would be required (or a reaction symbol added to the
action modifier/combat symbols).

>2) Can i play RoBR before a bloodhunt is called? And will it have any
>effect?

Yes, and yes.

>3) Can i use Heidelburg Castle before a bloodhunt is called? I
>remember someone answering no to that question. But I also remember
>another person saying that any master card (i.e. Fragment of book of
>Nood) can be tap during an action, to gain advantage of it's privilege.

In general, yes. Heidelberg Castle has specific cardtext restricting
when it can be tapped, however:

"Cannot be used during an action." (errata).

Section 6.5.5 of the revised rulebook gives 5 steps to the resolution
of diablerie:

1-Move all blood to the diablerist
2-Diablerist may take equipment
3-Victim is burned
4-Diablerist may gain a Discipline card if victim is older
5-Bloodhunt may be called.

Since this is part of the 'Diablerize in torpor' action, it's
clear you cannot use Heidelburg before the Bloodhunt if you're
sending in your vampire to diablerize as an action.

For diablerie a a result of blocking a self-rescue attempt (or
Rapid Healing, or Regeneration, or Movement of the Slow Body),
things are less clear, but I'd hazard that diablerie as a result
of blocking is similar to combat as a result of blocking, hence
part of the action, hence no Heidelburg.

gomi
